sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was two step changes rather than a smooth climb.
FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16.1 billion, with REGEN-COV contributing 66.4pp of that growth [D241][F6][D582], and FY2022 revenue fell 24.3% as REGEN-COV sales went to zero [D292][F7][S49].
The FY2021 surge reflected REGEN-COV sales under the September 2021 U.S. government supply agreement, which also lifted receivables by $1.93 billion [P39].
Since FY2022 the top line has grown only 5.6% a year to FY2025 [D767], while operating income fell at 8.9% a year over the same span [D769].
In FY2025 collaboration revenue of $7.33 billion, 51.1% of the total, contributed 9.0pp of the 1.0% revenue growth [S22][D521][D523][D440].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5.24 billion, driven by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][P9].
That was offset by U.S. EYLEA net product sales falling 42.4% to $2.75 billion, a 14.2pp drag on growth [S43][D577][D578], while EYLEA HD added 3.1pp [D614].
The EYLEA decline came from lower volumes on competitive pressure, share loss to compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition, plus a lower net selling price [P10].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4% [D464][D457], and net income grew 2.1% against diluted EPS growth of 8.2% as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D442][D444][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the margin as it rose to 40.8% of revenue, SG&A added 2.0pp as it fell 8.6%, and other lines cost 0.5pp [D465][D420][D466][D456][D467].

The SG&A decline was primarily lower charitable contributions to Good Days [P5], and gross margin on net product sales fell on manufacturing investment, inventory write-offs and higher Libtayo amortization [P4].
Net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin in FY2025 [F50][F30][D797], helped by other income of $1.65 billion [X117] against a 13.9% effective tax rate [D427].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income in FY2025, above the 1.10x window median [F80][F40][D428][D787], and free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x net income [F100][D429].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% window median [D425][D757], with capex at 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D424][D430].
Capex growth reflects the Tarrytown campus and Rensselaer fill/finish expansion, which the FY2023 filing flagged as continuing for several years [P19].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million absorbed 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16.9 billion, 117.7% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of the eight-peer group against a -50.7% median [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Cash and investments of $18.9 billion dwarf $1.99 billion of long-term debt [D432][F187], and the current ratio is 4.13x against a 3.97x window median [F180][D766].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.81 billion consumed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D436][D437], including a first dividend of $370 million [X140].
The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story, but return on average equity of 14.9% trails the 38.7% peer median [D439][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F27][F28][F29][F30][R1].
The compression is structural rather than cyclical: EYLEA, once 68.4% of revenue [D475], is shrinking while R&D runs at the 100th peer percentile [D778].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table, $5.15 billion and $6.56 billion, are later recasts against $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 -12.4% revenue growth [D92] should not be read as an operating result.
Whether U.S. EYLEA net product sales fall below the FY2025 level of $2.75 billion [S43], reported in the FY2026 10-K, would confirm the erosion described.
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 window low of 24.9% [F30][D749] in the FY2026 10-K would signal the cost trend has stabilized.
Whether R&D as a share of revenue stays above the 34.6% window median [D760] in the FY2026 10-K would show spending discipline has not returned.
